The model describes human IgG capture from a feed by protein A chromatography using AbSolute, a silica-based adsorbent. It predicts time-dependent movement and adsorption of IgG and impurities through a packed column, including breakthrough and elution behavior. The model combines axial transport and dispersion, finite-rate mass transfer, and adsorption equilibrium, with a saturation-dependent empirical mass-transfer correlation. The rapid-equilibrium steric mass action model represents protein binding and elution during strong cation-exchange chromatography. It predicts protein retention and outlet chromatograms by combining column transport, particle mass transfer, and SMA sorption, which represents competition between salt ions and proteins for binding capacity as well as protein shielding of binding sites. The paper compares estimating SMA parameters from gradient and breakthrough experiments with estimating them by inverse fitting of a mechanistic column model.
